chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does the menstruating woman enter into Ihram while she is not praying?' He said, 'Yes, when the time arrives, let her enter into Ihram.'
ai.seo_question: Does a menstruating woman need to enter Ihram if she cannot pray?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the obligation of Ihram is distinct from the ritual purity required for prayer, meaning a menstruating woman must enter the state of Ihram at the designated Miqat despite her exemption from Salat. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle that Ihram is a condition of the pilgrimage itself rather than a prerequisite of general ritual purity, ensuring the validity of the Hajj regardless of temporary impurity.
